title: Откровение Елены и подкат к Вике  (Elena's Revelation and Hitting on Vika)

segments.t: Touched by what the orderly told her, Elena walks into the ward and confesses to a thrilled Viktor Petrovich that she and her husband divorced after their son grew up. Meanwhile at Claude Monet, Aleksandr lures Vika into his office under the pretext of tasting a new dish.
В общем, по поводу моей семьи.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Yeah, help me out.' Replying firmly in front of Vika, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'This is our Viktoriya Sergeyevna.' Barinov replies promptly with a shrug, making his position completely clear.
'Oh, come on.' Barinov promptly chooses this word of agreement in the exchange using "ladno" ("alright") — built from the old Russian root for harmony and order, used every day for "okay, fine".
'I am just saying it in advance.' Turning evenly in the exchange, Vika links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'I am just kidding.' Barinov continues right away in this moment, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'To discuss a work matter.' Talking about the moment in the exchange, Vika chooses "rabochiy" ("working") so Barinov gets the point right away.
'Well, let us get to work.' Holding firm promptly in this beat, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Someone told me.' Vika speaks pointedly during the talk, leaving no doubt about where she stands.
В общем, по поводу моей семьи.
'Anyway, regarding my family.' Mentioning the matter right here, Barinov uses "obshchem" ("short, so", from "obshchiy") to make the point stick.
'I do not live with my husband anymore.' Pointing to her husband around Barinov, Vika chooses "muzhem" ("husband", from the root "muzh") so Barinov hears the exact meaning.
'Our son grew up, and we got divorced.' Barinov opens up boldly in this moment, without trying to dress up how he really feels.

'There just was never a right moment to mention it.' Turning to a right moment to Barinov, Vika puts the weight on "podkhodyashchego" ("suitable, fitting", from "podkhodyashchiy") as the exchange unfolds.
'Our new dish.' Checking on the dish in front of Vika, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
В общем, по поводу моей семьи.

That wraps up this scene as elena tells Viktor Petrovich that she is divorced and no longer lives with her husband, while at Claude Monet Aleksandr uses a new dish as an excuse to flirt with Vika. Until next time!
